arguments.value: 43-year-old man with prior presumed low-risk MDS presented with weakness, constipation, dry skin, leukopenia/anemia, cellulitis, and hypothyroidism. Initial concern for dermatomyositis/anti-synthetase syndrome due to mechanic’s hands/Gottron-like rash was unrevealing on autoimmune testing. Further history revealed heavy tororo kombu (seaweed) intake causing iodine excess and severe hypothyroidism with associated skin changes, constipation, weakness, and cytopenias; symptoms and labs improved after thyroid hormone replacement and stopping iodine-rich foods.
